issues.legal_issue: A grant of a minor inam comprising only part of a village does not qualify as an estate merely because it lies within a village granted as a whole to another holder.
material_facts: The inams were pre-settlement service and other minor inams, found to have been excluded from the assets of the zamindari at the permanent settlement.
The village itself was included in a grant of Mokhasa villages, and that grant was an estate; the minor inams were not grants of whole villages.
The tenants claimed permanent occupancy rights on the ground that the inams were part of an estate.
issues.conclusion: The minor inams were not estates, so the tenants could not claim statutory permanent occupancy rights on that basis.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 3(2)(d) of the Madras Estates Land Act, 1908, read with Explanation (1), the crucial test is whether the subject matter of the grant was a whole village or only part of one. A grant of a part of a village is not an estate; a grant expressed as one of a named village as a whole may qualify despite lands already granted on service or other tenure or reserved for communal purposes. The Court relied on District Board, Tanjore v. M. K. Noor Mohamed Rowther, A.I.R. 1953 S.C. 446, and applied Mantravadi Bhavanarayana v. Merugu Venkatadu, I.L.R. [1954] Mad. 116. Because the inams were not estates, section 6 did not give the tenants permanent occupancy rights.

predicates.occupancy_claim_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal in which a person claims occupancy protection on the basis that the land is part of an estate.
predicates.grant_was_whole_village: The grant covered the whole village that was its subject matter.
predicates.grant_was_expressed_as_whole_named_villa: The grant expressly identified a named village as the subject of the grant as a whole, rather than identifying only a defined area.
predicates.excluded_land_was_previously_granted_or_: Any land omitted from the named village grant had already been granted on another tenure or reserved for communal purposes.
predicates.statutory_occupancy_protection_unavailab: The claimant cannot obtain statutory occupancy protection on the basis that the grant was an estate.

issues.definition: When an occupancy-protection appeal concerns a grant that was neither of a whole village nor expressed as a whole named village with qualifying excluded land, statutory occupancy protection is unavailable.

issues.legal_issue: A concurrent factual finding is not disturbed on appeal when no special ground for interference is established.
material_facts: The lower courts concurrently found that the inams were pre-settlement grants excluded from the assets of the zamindari.
The appellants challenged that finding but did not establish a manifest error of law, disregard of judicial process, denial of fair hearing, or another special reason for revisiting it.
issues.conclusion: The Court left the concurrent finding undisturbed and proceeded on the basis that the inams were pre-settlement grants excluded from the zamindari assets.
issues.legal_principle: A concurrent finding of fact is not reopened on appeal without special grounds, such as a manifest error of law or disregard of judicial process or principles of fair hearing.

predicates.appeal_against_concurrent_factual_findin: The proceeding is an appeal challenging a factual finding reached concurrently by lower courts.
predicates.special_ground_for_interference: The appellant establishes a special reason to revisit the finding, such as a manifest error of law or disregard of judicial process or fair hearing.
predicates.concurrent_finding_left_undisturbed: The concurrent factual finding is not disturbed on appeal.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges a concurrent factual finding but no special ground for interference is established, the finding is left undisturbed.
